n: A gentle reply can calm someone’s anger; harsh words fan the flames. One of the most practical verses in Proverbs for family life and friendships.

f.w: A soft answer turneth away wrath

n: The wise use knowledge well when they speak; fools gush out foolishness.

f.g: Gushes, bubbles over like a spring.

n: God sees everywhere and watches both evil and good people. Nothing is hidden from him.

f.w: The eyes of the LORD are in every place

n: Healing words are like a tree of life; twisted words crush the spirit.

f.g: A wound or break in the spirit.

n: A fool rejects a parent’s discipline; whoever accepts correction shows good sense.

f.g: prudent = sensible, shrewd in a good way.

n: The home of the righteous holds real treasure; the earnings of the wicked bring trouble.
Wise people spread knowledge like a farmer scattering seed; the hearts of fools are not like that.

f.g: disperse = scatter, spread abroad, like seed.

n: God detests sacrifices offered by wicked people—worship without a changed life is empty. But the prayer of the upright delights him.

f.w: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination
the prayer of the upright is his delight

n: God detests the way of the wicked but loves those who pursue righteousness.
Discipline feels harsh to someone who has left the right path; refusing correction leads to death.
If even the underworld and the realm of destruction lie open before God, how much more can he see human hearts.

f.g: Hebrew Sheol and Abaddon—the grave and the place of destruction.

f.w: the hearts of the children of men

n: A mocker resents being corrected and avoids the wise.

f.w: neither will he go unto the wise

n: A happy heart shows on the face; heartache crushes the spirit. Inner life shapes outward appearance.
A discerning heart hungers for knowledge; a fool’s mouth feeds on foolishness. We become what we consume.
For the miserable every day is hard, but a cheerful heart enjoys a continual feast. Attitude changes how life is experienced.
Better to have little and revere the Lord than great wealth with turmoil.
A simple meal of vegetables with love is better than a feast of fattened beef with hatred. Relationships matter more than luxuries.

f.g: A plain vegetable meal—a poor person’s food.
A fattened ox kept in a stall—the finest meat.

n: A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict; a patient one calms a quarrel.
The lazy person’s path seems blocked by thorns—everything is an obstacle. The path of the upright is a smooth highway.
A wise child brings joy to a father; a foolish one shows contempt for a mother.

f.w: A wise son maketh a glad father

n: Folly brings joy to someone lacking sense, but a person of understanding keeps a straight course.
Plans fail without advice but succeed with many advisers.
It is a joy to give a fitting answer, and how good is a word at just the right time!

f.w: a word spoken in due season

n: The path of life leads upward for the wise, away from the grave below.

f.g: Sheol below—the grave, the realm of the dead.

n: The Lord tears down the house of the proud but protects the widow’s property lines. God defends the vulnerable.

f.g: Her boundary stones—powerful people sometimes moved them to steal land.

n: God detests evil thoughts, but gracious words are pure to him.
Greed for dishonest gain brings trouble on one’s household; whoever hates bribes will live.
A righteous person thinks before answering; the wicked blurt out evil.
The Lord is far from the wicked but hears the prayers of the righteous.

f.w: he heareth the prayer of the righteous

n: A bright face cheers the heart, and good news refreshes the body.
Whoever listens to life-giving correction will be at home among the wise.
Rejecting discipline is self-harm; accepting correction brings understanding.
Reverence for the Lord is the school of wisdom, and humility comes before honor. Jesus taught that the humble will be exalted.
